published_statement: Will 2014 eq.(62), p.43: 'A radar signal sent across the solar system past the Sun to a planet or satellite and returned to the Earth suffers an additional non-Newtonian delay in its round-trip travel time, given by  dt = 2(1+gamma) M_sun ln[ (r_E + x_E.n)(r_e - x_e.n) / d^2 ]  where x_e (x_E) are the vectors, and r_e (r_E) are the distances from the Sun to the source (Earth)' (TEGP 7.2); for a near-grazing ray dt ~ (1/2)(1+gamma)[240 - 20 ln(d^2/r)] microseconds (eq. 63). Will: 'Irwin Shapiro's 1964 discovery of this effect as a theoretical consequence of GR'. 1710.05834 eq.(3): dt_S = -(1+gamma)/c^3 * int_{r_e}^{r_o} U(r(l)) dl along the wave path (Shapiro 1964; Krauss & Tremaine 1988; Longo 1988) -- linear in the potential U.
published_hypotheses: PPN / weak-field, first post-Newtonian order: the delay is first order in M (in U); coefficient (1+gamma), gamma = 1 in GR
static (or uniformly moving, first order in v/c) point-mass source; Will sec. 4.1.3: moving-source correction is post^{3/2}-Newtonian (Kopeikin-Fomalont Jupiter 2002)
integral along the unperturbed straight line; d is the closest approach of that line to the source
round-trip radar form (factor 2 relative to one way); one-way form measured for PSR 1937+21 (Will p.43)
positive solar mass M_sun; no statement for M < 0
for extended sources 1710.05834 eq.(3) integrates the potential U along the path -- superposition, i.e. linearity in U
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED/MISAPPLIED (concentric.py:86-90, 325-328): the design rule 'shell delay / core advance ~ (L/R_s)/(2 ln(L/a))' and 'the core's advance carries a logarithm of its compactness' put the Plummer core radius a in the logarithm. The published form puts the CLOSEST APPROACH d of the straight line there; for the tree's own Plummer potential the first-order advance is 4m asinh((L/2)/sqrt(b^2+a^2)), i.e. ln(L/b) at the design point b = 1 >> a = 0.02. The a-form holds only on the smaller class b <~ a (ray through the core). Computed: exact first-order ratio 0.1315 (13.1 %) vs the owner's 0.0781 (7.8 %); the selftest check 'under 10 %' (concentric.py:327-328) and the rule 'make the core small' do not follow from Shapiro at b >> a (core advance/m = 22.8144 at a = 0.02 and 22.8152 at a = 0.002). The tree's own integrator agrees with ln(L/b): antisymmetric delay at m = 1e-3 is -1.98177e-2 against first-order ln(L/b) prediction -1.98144e-2 (ratio 1.0002) and against the ln(L/a) form -3.5463e-2 (ratio 0.559). Recorded as a discrepancy in the tree's use, not an error in the external result; the measured table (concentric.py:65-72) comes from integration, not from this formula, and is unaffected. Marked '~' by the owner (order-of-magnitude), which is why this is a discrepancy, not a refutation of 'nearly free'.

ADDED (composite.py:29, 52-53; concentric.py:6-7; specthm.py:1374-1381): extension to M < 0 ('the Shapiro delay, being linear, flips sign'). The published result states nothing for negative mass. Within the tree's prescribed linearised metric the first-order delay is exactly odd in M (sympy, S2) -- a mathematical property of the model, carried as a named hypothesis ('NEGATIVE MASS IS ASSUMED', composite.py WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED item 1); no datum exists for M < 0 either way.

WEAKENED/REINTERPRETED (composite.py:60-64, 342-344): the symmetric O(M^2) residue is attributed wholly to 'path lengthening of a bent ray'. In the tree's metric the null coordinate speed is 1 - 2Phi + 2Phi^2 + O(Phi^3) (sympy, S1), so an O(Phi^2) metric term also contributes; computed share 8.3e-5 of the 6.81e-3 residue (1.2 %). Attribution is right to ~99 %. Separately (named hypothesis, not checked here): the tree's metric is the LINEARISED one, so its O(M^2) residue is a statement about that model, not GR's second-order Schwarzschild delay; the published result is first order only and says nothing at O(M^2).
KEPT (composite.py:284-287): one-way form 2M ln[(x1+r1)/(x0+r0)] with gamma = 1 is exactly half of Will eq.(62) on the straight line, via (r0 - x0)(r0 + x0) = b^2 (sympy, S3). No drift.

KEPT (concentric.py:28-29): 'M_ADM = 0 makes the Shapiro gain CONVERGE' follows from linearity in U (1710.05834 eq.3): first-order integral of the tree's zero-monopole potential is 9.9825417 m at X = 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6 (rel. change 2e-11). No drift.

lacked_data: Shapiro in 1964 had no measurement of the effect at all -- it was a prediction; the data came later (Viking 0.1 % 1976, Cassini 1.2e-5 2003, Will 2014 p.43) and CONFIRMED the first-order form at gamma = 1, so on this result M's hypothesis runs the other way: the later data narrowed the uncertainty and moved nothing. What no one has, then or now, is any datum for M < 0; the tree's sign-flip use rests on the linearity of its prescribed metric (exact, S2), which is mathematics about the model, not physics confirmed by data -- a named hypothesis, neither supported nor refuted by measurement. The one discrepancy this audit finds is not in the external result and not caused by missing data: concentric.py puts the core radius where the published form puts the closest approach.
grade_evidence: The external result STANDS on its own terms and in composite.py's use: the one-way form is exactly half of Will eq.(62) at gamma = 1 (sympy S3), the straight-line integral is exact (S2), VALIDATION 3 reproduces at 0.6 % (T), and the only moved datum (gamma, Cassini) shifts it by <= 3.4e-5 (S4). It is graded NARROWED because concentric.py:86-90 and 325-328 use it on a class where it does not hold as applied: the logarithm's argument is taken as the core radius a, valid only for b <~ a, while the design point has b = 1 >> a = 0.02. Computed there: 13.1 % not 7.8 %, the 'under 10 %' check and 'make the core small' rule do not follow; the tree's own integrator sides with the published form (ratio 1.0002 vs 0.559). The M < 0 extension is an added hypothesis (named in composite.py as assumed), exact within the model. Not WRONG: nothing in the external result is refuted, and the owner's '~' marks an estimate -- this is a discrepancy recorded, not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: concentric.py's design rule restated with the closest approach (ln(L/sqrt(b^2+a^2))) or restricted to b <~ a -- i.e. the use brought inside the result's hypotheses. To OPEN on the O(M^2) side: if the tree were to quote its symmetric residue as GR's second-order delay (it does not now). To DATA-DEPENDENT: only a measurement of gamma departing from 1 at the 1e-2 level, excluded by Cassini at 1e-5. A fresh read of Shapiro 1964 itself (NAMED-NOT-READ here) could only change the source status, since Will's eq.(62) is the standard restatement.
